correctness.rationale: In the barycentric subdivision, ranks along a flag are distinct and preserved by D4. If points of the same closed flag simplex lie in one orbit, their support masks must match rank by rank, as must their coefficients. This gives injectivity on each closed simplex, not just pointwise stabilizers, and makes the flag-orbit cells regular. Orient by increasing rank; deleting different positions cannot identify faces because their rank sets differ. An independent enumeration from actual board masks found 24 attack edges, 1,364 nonempty independent faces, and flag-orbit counts (217,4801,35910,126666,239340,249840,136080,30240). A reverse-ordered free-face traversal checked unique live codimension-one cofaces, including maximality of the coface, and removed 411,365 pairs. The resulting core has (22,102,160,80) cells and no higher cells. Its integral boundaries compose to zero, with Smith ranks 21, 81 and 79 and all nonzero Smith factors one. The torsion of H_(d−1) equals that of coker ∂d, since the latter maps onto the free group im ∂_(d−1) with kernel H_(d−1). Thus the integral homology has one copy of Z each in degrees 0 and 3 and nothing else. A spanning tree and oriented triangle relators give a presentation in which all 81 generators are eliminated by Tietze moves. A separate reconstruction also matched the frozen certificate flag by flag and boundary by boundary. With π1 trivial, Hurewicz first gives π2=0 and then represents an H3 generator by a map S³ to the quotient. This map is an integral homology isomorphism between simply connected CW spaces and is a homotopy equivalence by homological Whitehead.
residual_risks: Proof uses exact finite enumeration of this board and the regular-cell and CW arguments above. It gives neither a homeomorphism with S³ nor a theorem for other squares or symmetry subgroups. Supplied executables were inspected, not run.

originality.rationale: The two closest earlier knight records give the same unquotiented wedge and rational D4 character, so the rational third Betti number of the geometric quotient is already determined. Neither classifies the ordinary orbit space up to homotopy. The closest same-day quotient records use king or bishop attacks and are not the same complex. The distinct contribution supported here is the integral sphere homotopy type of the ordinary knight orbit space.
residual_risks: The literature comparison is bounded and the Bode–Harborth primary scan was not read. The targeted web lookup was nondecisive and is not negative evidence; an unindexed equivalent remains possible.

value.rationale: The full square symmetry quotient of the first noncontractible square knight board is a natural exact invariant with a known rational baseline. The result determines that the rational sphere signature has no integral torsion and that the actual ordinary quotient is simply connected, giving its homotopy type. These data are not consequences of the old rational character or counts of placements and matter when comparing contrasts such as the king and bishop quotients on the same board.
residual_risks: The result is deliberately finite and provides no claim of PL type, equivariant type or a universal chessboard pattern.
